chunks: Jibrāʾīl, peace be upon him, descended upon the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and he said to him: “O Jibrāʾīl, advise me.”
He said to him: “O Muḥammad, live as you wish, for indeed you will die; love whomever you wish, for indeed you will part from him; and do whatever you wish, for indeed you will meet it.”
The honor of the believer is his salat (prayer) by night, and his dignity is in withholding harm from the people.

key_terms.صَلَاتُهُ بِاللَّيْلِ: his night salat (prayer), especially as an act of devotion
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: destined to die; a reminder of human mortality
key_terms.مُفَارِقُهُ: one who will part from what or whom he loves
key_terms.مُلَاقِيهِ: one who will meet the consequence of his deed

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about death, accountability, night prayer, and avoiding harm to others?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a concise exhortation on mortality, detachment from worldly attachments, and accountability for one’s deeds. It concludes by identifying night salat (prayer) as a source of the believer’s honor and refraining from harming others as a source of true dignity.
